title: The mixed coefficient is a relative derivation
statement: Let S be any scheme and G a group scheme over S [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let z:S[ε][δ]→G be a morphism over S, using the dual numbers [def-sc-dual-numbers], whose restrictions to δ=0 and ε=0 are the identity point. Put g=S→S[ε]→S[ε][δ]→G by setting both parameters to zero. There is a relative presheaf derivation D:𝒪_G→g_*𝒪_S over the pullback of 𝒪_S such that for every open V of G and section a, D(a) is the εδ coefficient of z♯(a).

source.place: Chapter 10, infinitesimal points; coefficient-extraction argument in Bracket.lean toMixed_bijective docstring

proof.text: Extracting the remaining single-parameter coefficient of either axis restriction gives zero. Equality of the base maps supplies the canonical transport between preimage opens; restrictions preserve these zero coefficients.

Define D componentwise as snd(snd(z♯(a))). Additivity follows from the section ring maps. Expanding multiplication gives the Leibniz law after the pure ε and δ coefficients vanish; the reduced map g supplies the constant coefficient. Naturality follows by applying snd twice to the naturality square of z♯.

Since z is over S, its composite with G→S equals the projection from the double thickening, whose section map has only a constant coefficient. By the pullback-pushforward adjunction the composite from the pullback base presheaf is fixed by the coefficient-killing endomorphism. Extracting snd twice shows D annihilates this composite. This verifies the relative derivation condition and the prescribed coefficient formula.
